predecessors.note: Kantoli has no Cliopatria row and no dossier; the page names it only in the infobox.

land.text: the Sumatran land of the Srivijaya shape of 1293 that Cliopatria's Majapahit shape of 1294 covers

successors.note: Cliopatria hands the land over in 1294: its Majapahit shape of 1294 holds 1,094 of the 1,500 cells of the last Srivijaya shape (Palembang, Jambi and West Sumatra among them) and its Malaya shape another 403. The pages opened give no annexation of Srivijaya by Majapahit in 1293-1294 (Majapahit is recorded at Palembang only in 1377, Melayu page).

successors.note: Cliopatria's Malaya row starts 1294; the Srivijaya page names the late-12th-century Malayu Dharmasraya kingdom of the Mauli dynasty as Srivijaya's successor, which is Sumatran, not peninsular.

capitals.name: Palembang
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Palembang' (no years). The page says the regional trading centre shifted from Palembang to Jambi without a year; the Melayu Kingdom page has Jambi leading the Sanfoqi missions from the 11th century. Treated as one seat for the map.

correction.text: The vicinity of Palembang, where Srivijaya 'was first established' (605 Saka, 683): Cliopatria's 674 shape held from 671

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts the Palembang core in 674, but the infobox gives 'Founded: c. 671' (the page dates Yijing's six-month visit to 671) and the Kedukan Bukit inscription is 'dated 16 June 682'. The shape is Cliopatria's 674 shape unchanged.
5,524 km2 around Palembang for 674-681; consistent with 'first established in the vicinity of today's Palembang'. No infobox area for these years.

170,101 km2 for 682-691: Jambi, Bangka and South Sumatra. The Kota Kapur inscription (28 February 686) is where Coedes' reading says the kingdom 'had just conquered the hinterland of Jambi and the island of Bangka'; Cliopatria draws the conquest from 682, the Kedukan Bukit year, so up to four years early. Kept.

483,627 km2 for 692-717. The Melayu page gives 'Annexed by Srivijaya: 692', which is Cliopatria's year; the Srivijaya page's infobox puts the conquest of Kedah at c. 682-685 (the shape reaches 7.0N, Kedah). The shape holds no cell of Banten, Jakarta or West Java, so the Tarumanagara page's 'coastal Banten and Jakarta areas came under Srivijayan control' is not drawn here.

537,553 km2 for 718-859, the shape that reaches 9.9N (the Isthmus of Kra, Chaiya/Ligor). The Srivijaya page says 'Langkasuka on the Malay Peninsula became part of Srivijaya' (7th century) and that Dharmasetu (c. 775) ordered three sanctuaries at Ligor; it does not date the step to 718. Infobox area is 1.2 M km2 for 1200 (see 1202).

Same 537,553 km2 as the previous row: Cliopatria re-dates the identical shape at 860 and the pages give no change then. The Srivijaya page lists missions to China in 853 and 871 under 'Melayu independence', yet Cliopatria keeps Jambi inside the shape until the early 13th century. fx-32 (F201): one date for the Melayu split, 1028. Melayu page (opened 2026-11-01): infobox 'Independence restored: 1028'; 'Sanfoqi sent a mission to China in 1028, but this would actually refer to Malayu-Jambi'; Jambi took 'the leadership of Sanfoqi from the 11th century onwards'. Srivijaya page (opened): 'after 1025 the term Sanfoqi referred to the Malayu Dharmasraya kingdom where the mandala was re-centred' and the 1028 mission 'would refer to Malayu-Jambi, not Srivijaya-Palembang', so from 1028 Palembang no longer holds the Melayu core; the page's 'Jambi became independent from Sanfoqi's influence in the early 13th century' is kept for the rest of the Jambi province (loss 1202). Ends 1027 here; 1028-1138 is srivijaya_1028.

ledger.note: 671: Srivijaya appears at Palembang. Infobox 'Founded: c. 671'; the page also dates Yijing's six-month visit to 671; the Kedukan Bukit inscription is 'dated 16 June 682' and 'dated 605 Saka (683), Srivijaya was first established in the vicinity of today's Palembang'.
c. 682-685: Srivijaya conquers Kedah. Infobox 'Conquest of Kedah: c. 682-685'. Cliopatria draws Kedah only from 692, and the Chola page (1025) shows the Srivijaya fleet based at Kedah.

region.text: the hinterland of Jambi and the island of Bangka

ledger.note: 686: the Kota Kapur stone is carved after a conquest. Dated '608 Saka (28 February 686 CE)'; Coedes: Srivijaya 'had just conquered the hinterland of Jambi and the island of Bangka'; the army 'just departed to attack Java, which is not submit to Srivijaya'.

region.text: the Melayu Kingdom, also called Jambi

ledger.note: 692: Melayu (Jambi) is absorbed. The Melayu page's infobox: 'Annexed by Srivijaya: 692'; Yijing (688-695) wrote that Malayu 'is now changed to Sribogha'. The Srivijaya page has Melayu 'the first kingdom to be integrated into Srivijaya' in the 680s, and the Kota Kapur page has the Jambi hinterland taken by 686.

region.text: the peninsula between Kedah and the Isthmus of Kra (Langkasuka, Ligor) added in Cliopatria's 718 shape

ledger.note: c. 718: Srivijaya reaches the Isthmus of Kra (Cliopatria's year; the page is silent on 718). 'Langkasuka on the Malay Peninsula became part of Srivijaya' (7th century); Maharaja Dharmasetu 'ordered the construction of three sanctuaries' at Ligor (c. 775).

region.text: Palembang and Kedah, the infobox 'Location: Palembang (Sumatra) and Kedah (Malay Peninsula)'

ledger.note: 1025: the Cholas raid Srivijaya. 'In 1025 AD, the Chola Emperor Rajendra I launched naval invasions on Srivijaya'; 'The first Srivijayan city to be attacked was Palembang, the empire's capital'; the Srivijaya navy at Kedah was caught unaware.

1026: the raids end with the king in Chola hands. Infobox 'Date: 1025-1026'; 'Rajendra Chola captured King Sangrama Vijayottunggavarman of Srivijaya'; the mandala is 'leaderless', and 'The Chola control over Srivijaya lasted for several decades'. No annexation: the page names no territorial change.

1028: Melayu-Jambi stands apart from Palembang again. Melayu page: infobox 'Independence restored: 1028' and 'Sanfoqi sent a mission to China in 1028, but this would actually refer to Malayu-Jambi'; Srivijaya page: 'after 1025 the term Sanfoqi referred to the Malayu Dharmasraya kingdom where the mandala was re-centred'. Mirrors melayu-kingdom ledger[2]. The rest of the Jambi province follows in 1202 (Srivijaya page: 'Jambi became independent from Sanfoqi's influence in the early 13th century').

Kedah (Kadaram), the land of Cliopatria's Sultanate of Kedah of 1139

ledger.note: 1139: Kedah leaves Srivijaya (Cliopatria's year; the pages opened are silent on 1139). The Srivijaya page has the Tamil poem Kalingatupparani of c. 1120 on 'Kulottunga's destruction of Kadaram' and the Chola page has the 1025 raid on Kedah, where the Srivijaya navy was stationed; Cliopatria's Sultanate of Kedah starts in 1139.

region.text: the peninsula north of Kedah, from Songkhla to Chaiya

ledger.note: 1139: the peninsula north of Kedah leaves Srivijaya (Cliopatria's year; page silent). The Chola page names Tambralinga as a rival kingdom that appealed to Srivijaya in 1025; the strip is the Songkhla to Chaiya coast. The reading that Tambralinga took it is mine.

c. 1202: Jambi leaves Srivijaya's orbit. 'Jambi became independent from Sanfoqi's influence in the early 13th century'; the year is the Cliopatria row boundary within that span. The Melayu page has Jambi leading the Sanfoqi missions from the 11th century and Malayu embassies to China in 1299 and 1301. fx-32 (F201): after the 1028 loss of the Melayu core this is the remainder of the Jambi province, the early-13th-century date of the Srivijaya page.

1288: Singhasari's expedition takes Palembang. The Melayu page: 'Mahesa Anabrang conquered Palembang and Jambi (Malayu)' in 1288, following the expedition decreed in 1275 (Pamalayu page: 'decreed in 1275, though perhaps not undertaken until later'). Hatched: the pages do not say Srivijaya was annexed.
1293: the expedition goes home. 'the expedition returned to Java on 3 May 1293'; the Mongol forces left Java on 23 April 1293. The Pamalayu page does not mention Palembang or Srivijaya.

1293: Cliopatria's Srivijaya ends, the year the Majapahit is founded. Page silent on any dissolution of Srivijaya: the Srivijaya page says only that 'The kingdom may have disintegrated after 1025'; the last epigraphic use of the name is a Chola inscription of 1030 or 1031 and the Melayu page has Majapahit crushing Palembang in 1377 as the end of 'efforts to revive Srivijaya'. The date is Cliopatria's.

wars.name: Srivijayan campaign against Java
belligerents: bhumi Jawa (the Java that did not submit; unnamed in the inscription)
wars.outcome: Outcome unrecorded: the inscription is carved as 'the Srivijaya army just departed to attack Java'.
wars.note: Infobox of the Srivijaya page: 'Dapunta Hyang Sri Jayanasa launched a military campaign against Java in the late 7th century'.

wars.name: Conquest of Kedah
wars.outcome: Kedah becomes Srivijayan (infobox 'Conquest of Kedah: c. 682-685').

wars.name: Mataram-Srivijayan wars
wars.outcome: No land changes hands: the Anjukladang inscription of 937, Dharmawangsa's naval invasion of 990 and Srivijaya's repulse of the Javanese in 1006; the infobox gives 'c. 937-1016'.
wars.note: The Mataram page dates the Wurawari attack on Mataram to 1016-1017.

wars.name: Chola invasion of Srivijaya
wars.outcome: Chola victory: King Sangrama Vijayottunggavarman captured, Palembang ransacked, the Srivijayan maritime monopoly broken.

wars.name: Pamalayu expedition
wars.outcome: Singhasari sends the expedition in 1275 (decreed) to Melayu; the Melayu page has Palembang and Jambi taken in 1288; the force returns to Java on 3 May 1293.
wars.note: Infobox 'Date: 1275-1292 (First phase)'. The Pamalayu page does not mention Srivijaya; the Melayu page does name Palembang.

certainty.note: A mandala of ports and river mouths; the pages give no frontier. The Cliopatria shape is a coastal envelope, and the Chola raids of 1025 and the 1288 expedition are point events.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Srivijaya' (674-1293) is read as one state: the pages opened give one Palembang-based kingdom whose reach and capital shift (Jambi from the 11th century) but not successive states, so it is not split. Its end is the open question: the Srivijaya page says it 'may have disintegrated after 1025', the last epigraphic mention is a Chola inscription of 1030-1031, Jambi leads the Chinese missions from the 11th century and goes independent in the early 13th, Singhasari takes Palembang in 1288 and Majapahit crushes a Palembang revival in 1377. 1293 is Cliopatria's year, kept as the end; a reviewer may prefer c. 1025-1031 or 1377. Area: infobox 1,200,000 km2 for 1200 against Cliopatria's 456,772 for 1202 (0.38); the shape is the coastal core. Sibling dossier tambralinga.json (written by another group from the Tambralinga page, not opened here) has Srivijaya occupying Tambralinga 775-969 and Tambralinga independent 970-1277, against Cliopatria's Srivijaya shape holding the Isthmus until 1138; the 718 and 1139 events here are Cliopatria's years at confidence 1 and a reviewer should prefer the Tambralinga page. Counterparts without a dossier: melayu-kingdom (Jambi/Dharmasraya, 671?-1347; the Melayu page), Kedah (Kadaram) before 1139, langkasuka, tambralinga, kantoli (infobox predecessor). Page budget (5) spent on Srivijaya, Kota Kapur, Chola invasion, Melayu, Pamalayu; not opened: Kedah, Tambralinga, Langkasuka, so the 692, 718 and 1139 shapes rest on Cliopatria's year with the page giving only the region. The Srivijaya page's account of Sailendra rule over Java and the Ligor inscription of c. 775 are not drawn. | fx-32 F201: Jambi/Melayu split dated 1028 (Melayu page, Srivijaya page on Sanfoqi re-centred on Malayu after 1025); keyframes 860/1139/1285 now subtract the Melayu core from 1028, 1202 loss kept for the rest of the Jambi province.
